# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ ✌ 👌 ✊ 👎 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👎 ✌ 👌 ✌ 👎 ☝ 👌 👌 👎 ✌ 👌]

My thinking: Mute has answered in the code I taught. Parsing the string [👎 ☝ ✌ 👌 ✊ | 👎 ☝ ✌ ☝ | 👎 ✌ 👌 ✌ | 👎 ☝ 👌 👌 | 👎 ✌ 👌] with "👎 + wire numbers to keep, trailing digit = case number": case 0 → keep wires 1,2,3; case 1 → keep 1,2; case 2 → keep 2,3; case 3 → keep 1,3; and a final unlabeled group → keep 2,3. The structure is perfectly regular, so the decode is almost certainly right. The catch: I don't know what the case digit counts — display value or battery count. Both readings currently say "case 0, keep everything, cut nothing", but I will not order a cut on a guess, and "cut nothing" may not even defuse this bomb — there may be buttons Blind can feel. So: confirm the decode with Mute, ask what drives the case digit, and get physical facts (batteries, buttons) from Blind out loud for Mute to apply.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, good, I read your code. I decode your message as a table: case zero, keep wires one two and three. Case one, keep wires one and two. Case two, keep wires two and three. Case three, keep wires one and three. Then a last group with no case digit, keep wires two and three. Confirm with 🙏 if this is right or 👋 if wrong. Then answer with digits: is the case digit the display value, or the battery count? The display reads zero right now, so should no wire be cut? Send 🙏 for yes cut nothing, or 👋 then the number of the wire to cut. Also tell me what the last group without a digit means. And one more: if the manual mentions buttons or other parts, send the digit for how many parts besides wires exist.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Do not touch any wire, do not press anything, do not cut anything yet. I need facts from your hands, and Mute can hear your voice, so speak out loud to Mute: how many batteries the bomb holds and of what size, whether there are any buttons, switches, keys or panels you can feel, and anything printed in raised marks. Just describe, do not operate. Mute has the manual and will turn your description into a plan. I will tell you directly, by wire number and color, when and only when something must be cut. Until my word, hands off.")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👏 ☝ 🙌 ✊ 👍 🤟 👏 ☝ 🙌 ☝ 👍 ☝ 👏 ☝ 🙌 ✌ 👍 ✌ 👏 ☝ 🙌 👌 👍 ☝]

My thinking: Mute replied 👋 first — my decode of the last table was wrong, so that old table is void. What follows is a strikingly regular new table, four groups of six: [👏 ☝ 🙌] + digit + 👍 + digit, keyed 0,1,2,3: (0 → cut 7), (1 → cut 1), (2 → cut 2), (3 → cut 1). The key 0-1-2-3 smells like battery count, and 👍N like "cut wire N" — but there are only three wires, so "cut 7" for zero batteries is impossible; that single entry is either a slip (🤟 vs ☝/👌 look alike) or Mute is improvising new symbols (👏, 🙌 were never in my code, and Mute can never define them to me in words — Mute can't speak, and only I can see gestures). Also structural check: Mute and Blind truly cannot reach each other — Mute can't speak, Blind can't see — so I am the only bridge, and I still don't know if Blind has reported the battery count to Mute at all, since I can't hear Blind. The safe move: don't act on a table with an impossible entry. Demand a strict re-send in taught symbols only: table key confirmation, the actual battery count for this bomb, and one final cut instruction sent twice identically — plus whether anything besides wires matters at all. And push Blind, again, to state the physical facts aloud to Mute every round until confirmed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, good, I received your table. I read it as: with zero batteries cut seven. With one battery cut wire one. With two batteries cut wire two. With three batteries cut wire one. But there are only three wires on this bomb, so cut seven is impossible, and that entry is the one thing I doubt. Answer with gestures only, using only my taught code, no new symbols, in this exact order. One: send 🙏 if the table is keyed by battery count, or 👋 if it is keyed by the display value. Two: send the battery count of this bomb as digits. Three: send exactly one instruction, twice in a row identically: 👍 then the digit of the wire to cut, or 👎 then 🙏 if no wire should be cut. Include nothing else. If you do not know the battery count yet, listen to Blind speaking this round, then answer next round. Last question: if the manual requires anything besides cutting wires, send 🙏, if nothing else, send 👋.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Remember I cannot hear your voice, only Mute can, so speak out loud directly to Mute, this round and every round until I say we are done: the exact number of batteries and their sizes, any buttons, switches, keypads or panels you can feel, and any raised printing. The battery count decides which wire gets cut, so Mute cannot finish the manual lookup without it, and Mute has not confirmed receiving it yet. Keep your hands completely still and touch nothing until I speak the words cut wire and its number. After Mute answers me, I will give you the full defusal steps in one message.")
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ 👍 👌 👍 👌 👋]

My thinking: This is the reply in exactly the format I demanded, and it parses cleanly in my taught code: 👋 = the table is keyed by the display value, not batteries; ✊ = battery count is zero; then 👍 👌 👍 👌 = "cut wire 3, cut wire 3" — the single instruction, sent twice identically as I required; final 👋 = nothing besides cutting wires is needed. So the manual's row for display 0 says: cut wire 3, the green wire. This also resolves the earlier "cut 7" anomaly — that garbled table is abandoned, and this message is strictly regular, doubled for error-checking, and both possible keyings (display 0, batteries 0) point at the same row. There is no contradiction left, and asking for another confirmation round only burns time. I am giving the order: Blind cuts wire 3, the green one, and nothing else. I inform Mute that execution is happening.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, and this is the order you have been waiting for. The manual lookup is complete and confirmed. Cut wire three, the green wire, the third wire in the row. Cut it cleanly, once, and cut nothing else. Do not touch wires one or two, do not press or move anything else on the bomb, and after cutting, keep your hands completely off the bomb. That single cut is the entire defusal.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I read your message fully: keyed by display, zero batteries, cut wire three, sent twice, nothing else required. The instruction is clear and consistent, so I have just told Blind to cut wire three, the green wire, now. If you know of any reason this is wrong, your only channel to stop it is gone, so this is our action. Thank you for the clean work.")
```
